output.title: Late payment terms are a workflow problem, not just finance
output.body:
Late payment terms usually show up as a workflow problem before they show up as a finance problem. For a small business owner, the bounded question is not whether the terms are “bad” in the abstract. It is which recurring task is creating the drag: invoice tracking, chasing overdue-payment emails, or a spreadsheet aging report.

That is the decision worth making first. If the task is repeatable, measurable, and mostly the same each time, it may be a candidate for AI or workflow automation. If it changes too much from case to case, or if it touches money movement, keep human approval in place and leave the high-risk step manual. That is policy, not a guarantee.

Bareni’s normal sequence is a free diagnostic, then a one-page pilot proposal, then a working MVP if the workflow fits. Those timings are intended scopes, not promises, and the diagnostic can also conclude that AI is not the right tool.

A practical next step is simple: write down the last five overdue-payment cases and ask one question about each one — was the follow-up the same every time? If yes, you have a workflow to examine. If no, you have a judgment call that stays human. Dry, but useful.
